commented.author: xiaocaidie313
commented.technical_background: Code review agent examples combine diff parsing, sandbox command execution, skill/tool selection, and persistent reports. The critical contract is that untrusted repository content and model-selected commands stay behind the advertised permission and sandbox boundaries.
commented.problem: The PR adds a skills-based Go code review agent example with fake and real LLM review paths, sandbox runners, diff parsing, SQLite storage, fixtures, and generated reports.
commented.necessity_assessment: The example is valuable for demonstrating a practical review workflow, but the safety model has to be correct because readers may copy it into real repositories.
commented.evidence_checked: Reviewed the current head diff for llmreview, sandbox runner, diff parser, storage/report surfaces, and file patches from the GitHub files API before posting comments.
commented.problem_framing: The main risks are execution authority and input trust: an LLM should not gain a command path outside the policy, and a sandbox should not receive unsanitized local repository contents.
commented.approach: The implementation wires llmagent skills, repository diff loading, sandbox command execution, and report persistence into a CLI example.
commented.implementation_derivation: The design is derived from the existing skill/tool execution model and codeexecutor workspaces, but the new example must narrow those generic capabilities for review-specific safety.
commented.solution_fit_assessment: The feature shape fits the example goal, while the current permission profile, repository staging, and unified-diff parsing leave correctness and security gaps.
commented.alternative_designs: A safer variant would use knowledge-only skill access plus a dedicated checked runner; repository staging can be based on tracked files and explicit changed files instead of whole-directory copy.
commented.tradeoffs: Restricting skill execution and sanitized staging adds setup code, but it keeps the example aligned with its own security claims and avoids leaking local artifacts.
commented.design_assessment: The example architecture is coherent, but it needs tighter boundaries before it can serve as a reliable reference implementation.
commented.modules: examples/skills_code_review_agent/internal/llmreview, internal/sandbox, internal/diff, CLI wiring, fixtures, and output report examples.
commented.api_surface: No library API is changed; the user-visible surface is an examples CLI and its skill/profile files.
commented.change_inventory: Adds a code-review-agent example with skill docs, LLM review path, sandbox runner, diff parser, storage, fixtures, and report outputs.
commented.semantic_changes: Introduces an example flow that can parse diffs, run checks, store findings, and optionally delegate review reasoning to an LLM.
commented.module_impact: Impact is scoped to examples, but copied patterns could influence downstream review tooling.
commented.cross_module_impact: Touches agent skill execution and codeexecutor concepts through example integration, without changing core packages.
commented.behavior_impact: Without fixes, LLM mode can escape the intended policy path, full repository staging can expose local files, and standard unified diffs can be silently ignored.
commented.tests_docs: Existing fixtures and tests cover several happy paths; additional coverage is needed for standard unified diffs and sanitized staging behavior.
commented.outcome: Posted three inline comments covering skill execution policy, repository staging hygiene, and standard unified diff parsing.

inline_comments.body:
`SkillToolProfileFull` exposes `skill_run`, but that execution path is not checked by this example's `PermissionPolicy`, so LLM mode can invoke arbitrary skill commands outside the advertised allow/deny and env whitelist. Use `SkillToolProfileKnowledgeOnly` here, or expose a purpose-built runner that applies the same permission policy before any command execution.
<details><summary>中文</summary>
`SkillToolProfileFull` 会暴露 `skill_run`，但这条执行路径没有走这个示例里的 `PermissionPolicy`，所以 LLM 模式可以绕过宣称的允许/拒绝策略和环境变量白名单去调用任意 skill 命令。这里建议改用 `SkillToolProfileKnowledgeOnly`，或者只暴露一个会先执行同一套权限校验的专用 runner。
</details>

`PutDirectory` stages the entire host repository for `--repo-path`, which can copy `.git`, ignored/untracked files, or local secrets into the sandbox. Stage a sanitized tree instead, for example tracked files from `git archive`/`git ls-files` plus explicit changed files, and exclude `.git`, ignored files, and secret patterns.
<details><summary>中文</summary>
`PutDirectory` 会把 `--repo-path` 指向的整个宿主机仓库放进 sandbox，这可能把 `.git`、被 ignore 的文件、未跟踪产物或本地密钥一起带进去。建议改成只放入清理过的文件树，例如 `git archive`/`git ls-files` 得到的 tracked files 加上明确选择的改动文件，并排除 `.git`、ignore 文件和常见密钥模式。
</details>

`--diff-file` can be a standard unified diff, but this parser only creates `current` after `diff --git`; a patch starting with `--- old` / `+++ new` produces no `FileChange`. Initialize a file change on `--- ` when `current` is nil, attach the `+++ ` path, and add coverage for non-git unified diffs.
<details><summary>中文</summary>
`--diff-file` 声称可以接收普通 unified diff，但这里只有遇到 `diff --git` 才会创建 `current`；如果 patch 直接以 `--- old` / `+++ new` 开头，就不会产生任何 `FileChange`。建议在 `current` 为空时遇到 `--- ` 也初始化文件变更，再用 `+++ ` 绑定新路径，并补上非 git unified diff 的测试。
</details>

commented.title: examples: add tool execution safety guard
commented.author: March-77
commented.technical_background: A tool execution safety guard classifies commands, working directories, environment, network access, and filesystem targets before a tool run. The contract is only useful if every execution field that can access protected paths is covered.
commented.problem: The PR adds an example safety guard for command execution with policies, samples, reports, and tests.
commented.necessity_assessment: The example addresses a real safety need for agent tool execution, but protected working directories must be enforced as part of the same policy.
commented.evidence_checked: Reviewed the guard policy structures, command classifier, forbidden path logic, samples, and current PR diff before posting the inline comment.
commented.problem_framing: Forbidden path checks currently treat the command string as the only access vector even though the request model includes a working directory.
commented.approach: The implementation parses command requests, applies deny/ask/allow rules, and emits audit/report artifacts for example scenarios.
commented.implementation_derivation: The guard derives safety decisions from policy arrays and regex classifiers, so each policy dimension has to map to the corresponding request field.
commented.solution_fit_assessment: The approach fits the example, but omitting `WorkingDir` from `ForbiddenPaths` breaks the promised directory protection.
commented.alternative_designs: The guard can normalize `WorkingDir` and compare it against protected paths, or resolve both command file references and working directory against an allowed workspace root.
commented.tradeoffs: Path normalization may need platform-specific care, but explicit working-directory enforcement is necessary for a safety example.
commented.design_assessment: The policy model is readable and extensible; it needs one more enforcement point to match its declared behavior.
commented.modules: examples/tool_safety_guard guard, policy JSON, samples, tests, and report examples.
commented.api_surface: No public package API is changed; this is an example module and CLI surface.
commented.change_inventory: Adds policy parsing, command classification, samples, audit output, and documentation for a tool safety guard.
commented.semantic_changes: The example introduces allow/ask/deny classification for tool execution requests.
commented.module_impact: Impact is scoped to the example, but the policy pattern may be reused by agent tool wrappers.
commented.cross_module_impact: No core runtime packages are changed; the example models how tool requests should be screened.
commented.behavior_impact: A harmless command can still run inside a protected directory, which bypasses the documented forbidden path policy.
commented.tests_docs: Add a case where `WorkingDir` points to a protected path while the command text itself is harmless.

commented.title: examples: add session replay consistency harness
commented.author: March-77
commented.technical_background: Replay consistency harnesses should execute the same operation sequence against multiple backends and compare loaded observable state. Saving a prebuilt final snapshot verifies serialization/comparison, not backend behavior.
commented.problem: The PR adds an examples/session replay consistency harness for sessions, memory, summaries, tracks, reports, and docs.
commented.necessity_assessment: The task is important because backend consistency bugs can hide until users switch storage implementations.
commented.evidence_checked: Reviewed the backend contract, replay scenario model, comparator, report output, and issue-oriented design claims before posting the inline comment.
commented.problem_framing: The harness currently bypasses the service APIs whose semantics it is supposed to compare.
commented.approach: The implementation defines snapshots, backend save/load hooks, comparators, and sample output for replay reports.
commented.implementation_derivation: A replay harness should derive expected state from operations, then let each backend produce actual state through the real service layer.
commented.solution_fit_assessment: The comparison and report shape are useful, but the backend interface needs to exercise actual session and memory APIs to satisfy the consistency goal.
commented.alternative_designs: Represent scenarios as operation lists and run them through adapters over `session.Service`, memory service, summary and track operations before normalization.
commented.tradeoffs: Operation-level replay is more code than snapshot save/load, but it catches semantic differences in create, append, update, delete, search, and persistence behavior.
commented.design_assessment: The report/comparator pieces are reasonable, while the backend abstraction is too high level for the stated test objective.
commented.modules: examples/session/replayconsistency backend contract, scenario data, comparator, report, README, and design doc.
commented.api_surface: No exported framework API changes; the new surface is an example module.
commented.change_inventory: Adds snapshot models, backend adapters, replay examples, comparison report, tests, and documentation.
commented.semantic_changes: The example is intended to compare backend-observable session and memory behavior across implementations.
commented.module_impact: Impact is scoped to examples but informs how future backend consistency checks may be written.
commented.cross_module_impact: The intended contract spans session, memory, summary, and track behavior even though the PR itself lives under examples.
commented.behavior_impact: Backends can disagree on real operations while still passing because both are handed the same final snapshot.
commented.tests_docs: Add operation-level cases that create sessions, append events, mutate memory, and compare loaded results.
commented.outcome: Posted one inline comment requiring operation-level replay through real backend APIs.

inline_comments.body:
`Save(Snapshot)` stores an already-final snapshot, so the replay only tests the comparator and not the real session/memory operation semantics from #2001. Drive each backend through the actual service APIs such as `CreateSession`, `AppendEvent`, summary/track/memory operations, then load and normalize the results for comparison.
<details><summary>中文</summary>
`Save(Snapshot)` 保存的是已经构造好的最终快照，这样 replay 实际只验证了 comparator，而没有覆盖 #2001 里要求的真实 session/memory 操作语义。建议让每个 backend 都通过真实 service API 执行，例如 `CreateSession`、`AppendEvent`、summary/track/memory 操作，然后再 load、normalize 并比较结果。
</details>

commented.author: March-77
commented.technical_background: Prompt optimization gates compare candidate prompts against baseline metrics and optional budgets. Optional JSON budget fields need explicit absent handling so defaults do not silently change policy.
commented.problem: The PR adds a prompt optimization regression loop example with datasets, candidate prompts, metrics, report output, and a deterministic pipeline.
commented.necessity_assessment: The example is useful for showing safe prompt iteration, but omitted budget fields must not become strict zero budgets.
commented.evidence_checked: Reviewed the gate config, pipeline decisions, data files, tests, and report generation before posting the inline comment.
commented.problem_framing: Numeric zero is both a valid configured budget and the Go zero value for an omitted JSON field, so the current gate cannot distinguish absent from explicitly configured.
commented.approach: The implementation loads evaluation traces, compares baseline and candidate metrics, applies gates, and emits optimization reports.
commented.implementation_derivation: The gate logic is derived from score deltas, critical cases, hard-failure checks, cost budgets, and tool-call budgets.
commented.solution_fit_assessment: The regression-loop structure fits the example, but budget fields need nullable or post-decode defaults to keep configuration semantics correct.
commented.alternative_designs: Use pointer fields for optional budgets, or keep value fields and fill absent values with negative disabled sentinels during config normalization.
commented.tradeoffs: Pointer fields make absence explicit; sentinel defaults keep call sites simple but require a clear normalization step.
commented.design_assessment: The deterministic pipeline is clear; optional configuration semantics need tightening.

`MaxCostIncrease` and `MaxToolCalls` decode as zero when omitted, but the `>= 0` gates then reject any cost increase or any tool calls. Make these optional pointers or set absent fields to a disabled sentinel after decoding, and enforce the budgets only when explicitly configured.
<details><summary>中文</summary>

commented.title: examples: add sandboxed code review agent
commented.author: March-77
commented.technical_background: A sandboxed code review agent ingests diffs or repository changes, runs static rules, may execute checks in an isolated runtime, and emits findings. Its example value depends on matching the declared sandbox, input, and security-rule contracts.
commented.problem: The PR adds a sandboxed code review agent example with diff parsing, rules, container execution, storage, reports, skill files, and fixtures.
commented.necessity_assessment: The example can be useful, but the current implementation leaves several security and correctness holes in the advertised workflow.
commented.evidence_checked: Reviewed the Dockerfile, repository diff loading, secret detection rules, sandbox workspace creation, diff summary logic, and relevant codeexecutor runtime behavior before posting comments.
commented.problem_framing: The issues cluster around environment compatibility, incomplete input capture, insufficient secret matching, unenforced workspace limits, and inaccurate deleted-file summaries.
commented.approach: The implementation builds a CLI around repository/diff inputs, rule execution, optional container sandboxing, SQLite storage, and markdown/JSON reports.
commented.implementation_derivation: The design follows a common review-agent pipeline: normalize input, parse diff, run rules, optionally run checks, store task state, and render a report.
commented.solution_fit_assessment: The pipeline shape fits the goal, but the current details do not yet satisfy the safety and correctness contract of a sandboxed review example.
commented.alternative_designs: Use a Go version aligned with the module, synthesize diffs for untracked files, broaden secret regexes, enforce pre-copy workspace size, and count deleted-file hunks in summaries.
commented.tradeoffs: The fixes add validation and fixture complexity, but they prevent clean reports that miss real files or security findings.
commented.design_assessment: The example is comprehensive, but several boundary conditions need repair before it can be treated as a reference.
commented.modules: examples/code_review_agent Dockerfile, input loader, rules, container sandbox, diff parser, storage, reports, skill files, and fixtures.
commented.api_surface: No framework API changes; the user-visible surface is the example command and generated reports.
commented.change_inventory: Adds a complete example agent with sandbox runner, static rules, persistent task records, fixtures, and report artifacts.
commented.semantic_changes: The example introduces repository/diff review behavior and optional sandbox execution for changed code.
commented.module_impact: Impact is scoped to examples, with likely reuse by developers building local review automation.
commented.cross_module_impact: The example depends on codeexecutor workspace behavior and demonstrates integration rather than changing core runtime code.
commented.behavior_impact: The current version can fail in container mode, miss untracked files and short-declared secrets, copy oversized repositories before limits, and undercount deletions.
commented.tests_docs: Add fixtures for untracked files, short-declared secrets, deleted-file summaries, and container Go version compatibility.
commented.outcome: Posted five inline comments covering Go version mismatch, untracked input files, secret regex gaps, workspace size enforcement, and deleted-file summary counting.

inline_comments.body:
`go.mod` requires Go 1.24.0 while this sandbox image installs Go 1.23 and the runner sets `GOTOOLCHAIN=local`, so container checks can fail before the example runs. Use a Go 1.24+ base image, or lower the module directive only if the code is actually compatible.
<details><summary>中文</summary>
`go.mod` 要求 Go 1.24.0，但这个 sandbox 镜像安装的是 Go 1.23，而且 runner 设置了 `GOTOOLCHAIN=local`，所以 container 模式可能在示例真正运行前就失败。建议换成 Go 1.24+ 的基础镜像；如果代码确实兼容更低版本，再考虑降低 module directive。
</details>

`git diff HEAD --` ignores untracked files in `--repo-path` mode, so a newly created Go file with secrets or unsafe code can yield an empty clean report. Include untracked files via `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard` and synthesize diffs for them, or reject untracked files explicitly.
<details><summary>中文</summary>
`--repo-path` 模式下的 `git diff HEAD --` 不会包含未跟踪文件，所以新建的 Go 文件即使包含密钥或不安全代码，也可能得到空的 clean report。建议用 `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard` 收集未跟踪文件并合成 diff，或者明确拒绝存在未跟踪文件的输入。
</details>

`:=` declarations are missed by these secret regexes, so common Go code like `apiKey := "..."` or `token := "..."` passes the required hardcoded-secret rule. Accept both `=` and `:=` in the patterns and add fixtures for short declarations.
<details><summary>中文</summary>
这些密钥正则没有覆盖 `:=` 短变量声明，所以常见的 Go 写法如 `apiKey := "..."` 或 `token := "..."` 会绕过必需的硬编码密钥规则。建议让模式同时支持 `=` 和 `:=`，并增加短变量声明的 fixture。
</details>

`MaxDiskBytes` is passed to `CreateWorkspace`, but the container/E2B workspace runtimes currently ignore `WorkspacePolicy`, so oversized repositories are still copied before any size guard. Enforce a pre-copy size/exclusion limit in `ContainerSandbox` or use a runtime path that actually applies `MaxDiskBytes`.
<details><summary>中文</summary>
这里把 `MaxDiskBytes` 传给了 `CreateWorkspace`，但当前 container/E2B workspace runtime 会忽略 `WorkspacePolicy`，所以超大的仓库仍然会在大小限制生效前被复制进去。建议在 `ContainerSandbox` 里复制前先做大小/排除规则校验，或者改用真正会执行 `MaxDiskBytes` 的 runtime 路径。
</details>

`DiffSummary` increments the file count for deleted files and then skips their hunks, so deleted-file reports show `-0` even when lines were removed. Count `LineRemoved` hunks for deleted files before continuing and add a deleted-file summary test.
<details><summary>中文</summary>
`DiffSummary` 对删除文件只增加文件数就跳过 hunk，因此即使删除了很多行，报告里也会显示 `-0`。建议在跳过前统计删除文件里的 `LineRemoved` hunk，并补一个删除文件摘要的测试。
</details>
